question.problem:
Given the joint probability distribution for two discrete random variables $X$ and $Y$ below, find $\text{E}[X].$

| $f$ | $Y=1$ | $Y=2$ | $Y=3$ |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| $X=-1$ | $0.05$ | $0.05$ | $0.2$ |
| $X=1$ | $0.15$ | $0.1$ | $0.15$ |
| $X=3$ | $0.15$ | $0.05$ | $0.1$ |
question.worked_solution:
Recall that the marginal distribution for $X$ corresponds to the row totals, and the marginal distribution for $Y$ corresponds to the column totals.

| $f(x,y)$ | $Y=1$ | $Y=2$ | $Y=3$ | ${f}_{X}$ |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| $X=-1$ | $0.05$ | $0.05$ | $0.2$ | $0.3$ |
| $X=1$ | $0.15$ | $0.1$ | $0.15$ | $0.4$ |
| $X=3$ | $0.15$ | $0.05$ | $0.1$ | $0.3$ |
| ${f}_{Y}$ | $…$ | $…$ | $…$ | $1$ |

Therefore, the probability mass function for  $X$ is given by the following table:

| $x$ | $-1$ | $1$ | $3$ |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| ${f}_{X}(x)$ | $0.3$ | $0.4$ | $0.3$ |

Finally, the  expected value of $X$ is 

$$
\begin{aligned}\text{E}[X] & ={\sum }_{i=1}^{n}{x}_{i}\,{f}_{X}({x}_{i}) \\  & =(-1)\cdot 0.3+1\cdot 0.4+3\cdot 0.3 \\  & =-0.3+0.4+0.9 \\  & =1.\end{aligned}
$$
